newsitem.title: FRANCE: French welfare system to be in deficit in 97.
newsitem.headline: French welfare system to be in deficit in 97.

text.p: French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said the government was succeeding in taming health care spending but would be unable to achieve its goal of eliminating the country's welfare deficit in 1997.

"It's clear we will have a social security deficit in 1997. Our goal -- which was to return to breakeven in 1997 -- will be delayed until the end of 1997 or early 1998," Lamassoure, who is also budget minister, said on French radio RTL.
Lamassoure said, however, the 1996 social security shortfall would likely be lower than the 55 billion francs suggested by various newspaper reports.
The government predicted last year a social security deficit of 16.6 billion francs for 1996 and a surplus of 11.8 billion francs in 1997.

He said overshooting the deficit would not interfere with the goverment's aim of reducing the total public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product by 1997 to qualify for European monetary union.

Lamassoure, blaming the social security shortfall on lower than expected payroll tax receipts as a result of a slow economy, said the government would eliminate the deficit by implementing various savings measures.
